basis: Extraskeletal chondroma arising within the CNS, usually from the dura; cartilage histology does not establish skeletal involvement.
Newcastle virus infection; conjunctivitis, respiratory illness and diarrhea are generally transient, without common lasting organ injury.
Persistent neurodevelopmental impairment defines this umbrella concept; additional organ abnormalities vary by underlying disorder.
Microcephaly and developmental/intellectual disability are core features; structural digital abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Facial and pinna differences do not establish functional organ damage.
Malignant neoplasm originating in intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts, both covered by the hepatic axis.
Motor axonal neuropathy in 15/15; muscle wasting in 10/17 and fixed contractures in 9/17 establish common musculoskeletal damage.
Microcephaly and progressive axonal polyneuropathy define the syndrome; progressive muscle wasting and scoliosis are characteristic manifestations.
Acquired oxidation of hemoglobin defines this blood disorder; hypoxic symptoms and acidosis do not establish lasting damage to additional organs.
Autoimmune hemolysis occurs in 50-75%; pericarditis in 2/2. Recurrent gastroenteritis represents separate infection; restrictive physiology alone does not establish direct lung damage.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy and pes cavus occur in nearly all reported patients, hearing impairment in 30-79%. Pupil abnormalities alone do not establish eye damage.
Familial hemiplegic migraine is a neurological disorder; transient motor deficits do not establish damage to additional organs.
Carcinoma arising from the exocrine pancreatic ducts; exocrine pancreas belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Astrocytic neoplasm originating in the brain stem.
HIV-associated inflammation of CNS arteries defines a cerebral vascular and infectious/immune disorder.
Inflammatory retinal vasculitis with venous occlusion and vitreous hemorrhage defines the disease; neurological injury is uncommon.
Pudendal nerve neuropathic pain defines the condition; urinary, rectal and genital symptoms do not establish direct damage to those organs.
Tumor originating in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in the larynx; the pulmonary axis includes the laryngeal airway.
Mature T-cell lymphoma originating in skin; lymphoid blood-cell neoplasia and the lymphoma mechanism also apply.
Cerebellar malformation and neurodevelopmental impairment define Joubert syndrome; AHI1-associated retinal dystrophy occurs in roughly 70-80%. Renal disease affects a minority.
Progressive diaphyseal hyperostosis defines this skeletal dysplasia. Hypogonadism and mitral valve abnormalities lack established frequency or diagnostic status in this single-family disorder.
Hydrocephalus with cerebral aqueductal dysgenesis and craniosynostosis directly defines brain and skull involvement.
Inflammation of the larynx and trachea, typically infectious; infectious ancestry and the croup subtype support the mechanism axis.
Umbrella disorder of porphyrin metabolism; neurological and cutaneous damage differ across subtypes and do not reliably apply to most patients across the group.
Lysosomal storage disease; intellectual disability, scoliosis and gingival overgrowth each occur in 80-99%, dental abnormalities in 30-79%. Hepatosplenomegaly is below 30%.
